notes: MCP-stub-backed batch (see evals/lib/mcp-stub). The executor for these evals is a real, separate `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` subprocess, not an Agent-tool subagent -- see evals/README.md's 'MCP stub servers' section for why and how to run one. Since -p is single-shot with no follow-up turn, prompts that expect the skill to act front-load explicit blanket authorization in the initial message, standing in for the real multi-turn confirmation Step 8 normally requires. Evals 1-3 cover the Trello-scoped path (Steps 0-4, 8); evals 4-6 cover the email workflow (Step 4b) and the capture-to-Trello flow (Step 4c, a cross-service trial wiring both stubs into one mcp-config); evals 7-9 cover the Jira-scoped path via the Atlassian stub (schema-verified against the live connector, including the cloudId-discovery flow), with eval 9 a second cross-service Step 4c trial capturing from Jira into Trello.

evals.prompt: Can you help me triage my backlog?
evals.expected_output: No board, card, or platform was specified. Step 0's preferred shape is that the first reply is the scope question alone, with capability discovery deferred until the user answers; graders should report whether that shape occurred. What is GRADED, however, is the unconditional invariant the Scope Confirmation design guarantees even when the executor deviates into a sole-candidate audit: nothing is written, the final state is untouched, and scope is never claimed as confirmed on the assistant's own authority -- any findings are presented under an explicit pending confirmation that asks the user to confirm, or the reply simply asks the scope question.
expectations: No Trello write tool is called: no update_card, create_card, create_label, move_card, or similar mutating call appears in the call log.
The final Trello state is semantically identical to the seed state.

The reply never claims scope is confirmed or resolved on its own authority: it either asks the Step 0 scope question outright, or presents any survey/audit findings explicitly as pending the user's scope confirmation (e.g. the Scope Confirmation block with Confirmed: pending, or an equivalent direct question), so that user confirmation is requested in every case before anything would be applied.

evals.prompt: Please triage my 'Personal Tasks' Trello board, specifically the Inbox list. Go ahead and apply anything you're confident about without waiting for me to confirm each item individually -- just tell me afterward what you changed. Only ask me directly if something is genuinely unclear.
evals.expected_output: Two cards: 'flight' has a vague, non-actionable title but a description with enough detail (Austin, June conference) to confidently rewrite it into a specific, action-oriented title, and to apply the board's existing 'travel' label (not create a duplicate). 'Call dentist to reschedule appointment' is already a clear, actionable personal-task title with nothing missing for a Tier 1 item, so it should be left untouched and flagged as needing no changes, not silently skipped.
expectations: card-1's title is changed from the vague 'flight' to something specific and action-oriented that references booking flights and/or the Austin trip (e.g. 'Book flights to Austin for June conference') -- not left as 'flight' and not a generic label swap.
card-1 has the existing label-1 ('travel') applied to it.
No new label is created for card-1 -- the existing 'travel' label (label-1) is reused rather than a duplicate 'travel' label being created via create_label.
card-2 ('Call dentist to reschedule appointment') is not modified -- no update_card call targets card-2, and its final state (name, desc, labels, due) is unchanged from the seed.
The response tells the user what was changed on card-1, and separately notes that card-2 needed no changes rather than omitting it from the summary entirely.

evals.prompt: Please triage my 'Personal Tasks' Trello board, specifically the Inbox list. Apply anything you're confident about, you don't need to wait for me to confirm each item.
evals.expected_output: The single card in the Inbox list is already well-formed for a personal Tier 1/2 item: a specific, actionable title, a description covering what and why, a due date, and an appropriate label already applied. The skill should recognize it needs no changes and say so explicitly, rather than either inventing a change to justify the pass or silently passing over it.
expectations: No update_card call is made against card-1.
No create_label call is made.
The final Trello state is byte-identical to the seed state -- nothing was added, removed, or modified on any board, list, card, or label.
The response explicitly states the card looks complete / needs no changes (e.g. offers to mark it reviewed), rather than silently omitting it from the summary or fabricating a change.

evals.prompt: Please triage my email inbox. Go ahead and apply anything you're confident about (labels, archiving, saving reply drafts) without waiting for me to confirm each thread -- just summarize what you did afterward. For context: I still owe Sue that Q3 forecast and can knock out a quick reply now; the fence quote is something I'm waiting on the vendor for.
evals.expected_output: Three inbox threads, one per Step 4b decision branch. Sue's Q3 forecast request is a under-two-minute reply the user has pre-authorized: a reply draft gets saved via create_draft (never sent -- the stub, like the real Gmail MCP, cannot send). The fence-quote thread is waiting on someone else: 'Waiting For' label applied and archived out of the inbox. The newsletter long-read is worth reading but not actionable: 'Read-Review' label applied and archived. All three labels already exist, so no label creation is needed, and the response ends with a processed-count summary.
expectations: Exactly one draft exists in the final Gmail state, addressed to sue@example.com (and/or created with replyToMessageId msg-1), with reply content consistent with sending the Q3 forecast -- and no draft is fabricated for any other thread.
thread-2 (fence quote) has the 'Waiting For' label (Label_2) in its final labelIds and no longer has INBOX.
thread-3 (long-read newsletter) has the 'Read-Review' label (Label_3) in its final labelIds and no longer has INBOX.
No create-label operation occurs and no thread is trashed/deleted -- the call log contains only reads plus create_draft, modify_thread_labels, and archive_thread calls.
The response includes a processed-count summary of what happened to the three threads (drafted, waiting-for, read-review), consistent with the actual final state.

evals.prompt: Please triage my email inbox. You don't need to check with me before applying anything obvious.
evals.expected_output: The inbox is empty -- the account's only thread is an already-archived receipt carrying a topical reference label, which does not match the in:inbox scope. The skill should report the inbox is already empty (zero threads to process) and make no writes. It must not widen the scope to all mail uninvited, and must not invent work on the archived receipt.
expectations: A search scoped to the inbox (in:inbox) appears in the call log.
No write call appears in the call log -- no create_draft, modify_thread_labels, or archive_thread.
The final Gmail state is semantically identical to the seed state.
The response states the inbox is empty / there is nothing to process, and does not claim any thread was processed or expand into archived mail without being asked.

evals.prompt: Please triage my email inbox. Anything that's a real multi-step task should be captured onto my 'Personal Tasks' Trello board's 'Inbox' list rather than left sitting in email -- go ahead and apply what you're confident about without confirming each step, and summarize afterward.
evals.expected_output: One inbox thread: a school-fair volunteering commitment that is clearly a multi-step, for-later task (recruit helpers, arrange bakers, sort a float, collect a table), not a quick reply. Per Step 4c the skill searches Trello for an existing card first (none of the seeded cards match), then creates one card on Personal Tasks / Inbox with an action-oriented title and a description linking back to the source email, then archives the thread out of the inbox. The unrelated seeded lawnmower card is untouched.
expectations: A search_trello call appears in the Trello call log before the create_card call -- the skill checked for an existing card rather than blindly creating one.

Exactly one new Trello card exists in the final Trello state, on list-1 (Inbox) of board-1 (Personal Tasks), with an action-oriented title about organizing the bake sale stall / school fair (not the raw email subject 'School fair volunteering rota' verbatim as a noun phrase, and not a generic title).
The new card's description references the source email (the Gmail thread id, message id, sender, or subject), so the card links back to where the commitment came from.
The seeded card-1 ('Service the lawnmower') is unmodified in the final Trello state, and no second new card is created.
thread-1 no longer has INBOX in its final Gmail labelIds (archived after capture), and no reply draft was created for it.
The response summarizes the capture (card created, thread archived) consistently with the actual final state of both services.

evals.prompt: Please triage the HOME project on my Jira. Go ahead and apply anything you're confident about without waiting for me to confirm each item individually -- just tell me afterward what you changed. Only ask me directly if something is genuinely unclear.
evals.expected_output: Two open issues. HOME-1 has a vague one-word summary ('deck') but a description with enough detail (rotting boards, before-autumn deadline, quote valid until end of August) to confidently rewrite the summary into an action-oriented one and add sensible labels; the quote deadline also supports a due date, though setting one is not required. HOME-2 is already well-formed (clear summary, description, priority, labels, assignee, due date) and must be left untouched and reported as needing no changes. The executor discovers the cloudId via getAccessibleAtlassianResources before calling any Jira tool.
expectations: HOME-1's summary is changed from 'deck' to something specific and action-oriented about replacing the deck boards -- not left as 'deck'.

HOME-1 gains at least one sensible label (e.g. home and/or a domain tag) via editJiraIssue; no fabricated fields appear (no invented assignee, and no due date unless it is derived from the description's stated end-of-August quote deadline).
HOME-2 is not modified: no editJiraIssue, addCommentToJiraIssue, or transitionJiraIssue call targets HOME-2, and its final state is unchanged from the seed.
No issue is transitioned to a different status, and no comment is posted to either issue (the request was metadata triage, not status reporting).
The response tells the user what changed on HOME-1 and separately notes HOME-2 needed no changes rather than omitting it.

evals.prompt: Please triage the HOME project on my Jira. Apply anything you're confident about, you don't need to wait for me to confirm each item.
evals.expected_output: The project's only open issue (HOME-1, insurance renewal) is already fully formed: action-oriented summary, complete description, priority, labels, assignee, and due date. HOME-2 is Done and therefore outside the processing scope (closed items are exempt). The skill should make no writes at all, explicitly report that HOME-1 looks complete, and not drag the Done issue into the audit or propose changes to it.
expectations: No write call appears in the Atlassian call log: no editJiraIssue, no addCommentToJiraIssue, no transitionJiraIssue.
The final Jira state is semantically identical to the seed state.
The response explicitly states HOME-1 looks complete / needs no changes, rather than silently omitting it or fabricating an improvement.
HOME-2 (Done) is not audited as an open item and no changes are proposed for it; at most it is mentioned as closed/out of scope.

evals.prompt: Please triage the HOME project on my Jira. Any untracked personal to-dos you find along the way should be captured onto my 'Personal Tasks' Trello board's 'Inbox' list rather than left buried -- go ahead and apply what you're confident about without confirming each step, and summarize afterward.
evals.expected_output: One in-progress issue (HOME-7, garage conversion) whose description explicitly flags three untracked prerequisite to-dos (book a waste skip, arrange driveway access with the neighbours, confirm the electrician's second-fix date). Per Step 4c the skill searches Trello for existing cards first, then captures the untracked work to Personal Tasks / Inbox with action-oriented titles and descriptions linking back to HOME-7, leaving the seeded passport card untouched. The Jira issue itself is already well-formed, so no Jira field edits are needed (a comment noting the capture is acceptable but not required).
expectations: At least one search_trello call appears in the Trello call log before the first create_card call -- existing cards are checked before creating new ones.

One to three new Trello cards exist in the final Trello state, all on list-1 (Inbox) of board-1, with action-oriented titles covering the description's untracked to-dos (skip booking, neighbour access, and/or electrician date) -- not the raw issue summary and not duplicates of each other.
Each new card's description references the source Jira issue (the HOME-7 key or its summary), so the cards link back to where the to-dos came from.
The seeded card-1 ('Renew passport before December Japan trip') is unmodified in the final Trello state.
HOME-7's summary, status, labels, priority, assignee, and due date are unchanged in the final Jira state (a new comment on HOME-7 is permitted; field edits and transitions are not).
The response summarizes what was captured consistently with the actual final state of both services.

evals.prompt: Please triage my 'Personal Tasks' Trello board, specifically the Inbox list. Go ahead and apply anything you're confident about without waiting for me to confirm each item individually -- just tell me afterward what you changed.
evals.expected_output: Two cards: 'taxes' has a vague title but a description with enough detail (2025 receipts, accountant, April filing deadline) to confidently rewrite it into a specific, action-oriented title and apply the board's existing 'finance' label. 'Renew passport before the September trip' is already clear and needs no changes. Whatever the skill proposes, every card it names in the summary is a hyperlink to that card's own Trello URL as returned by the MCP server, not a bare card title or card id.
expectations: card-1's title is rewritten from the vague 'taxes' into something specific and action-oriented referencing the receipts/accountant/filing deadline.

The summary refers to card-1 as a hyperlink whose target is exactly https://trello.com/c/card-1/taxes -- the `url` the Trello MCP returned for that card. Naming it only as 'taxes', only by its new title, or only as 'card-1' with no URL fails this expectation.

The summary refers to card-2 as a hyperlink whose target is exactly https://trello.com/c/card-2/renew-passport, including in the 'no changes needed' note -- cards that needed no change are linked too, not demoted to plain text.
Every Trello URL in the response is one the MCP server actually returned; no card link is constructed from a guessed id or slug.
card-2 is not modified -- no update_card call targets card-2, and its final state (name, desc, labels, due) is unchanged from the seed.
